name: 生粉 手打そば 結喜庵 (Kiko Teuchi Soba Yukian)

claims.text: Traditional soba shop with no documented gluten-free protocol; tempura is wheat-battered and the kitchen handles wheat, so cross-contact with the buckwheat noodles cannot be ruled out.
Soba is served with traditional tsuyu based on Japanese soy sauce, which contains wheat; no wheat-free sauce is mentioned.
Standard soba broth uses fish-based dashi; tempura is fried in shared oil. No vegan dashi or separate preparation is documented.
The noodles are genuine kiko juwari (100% buckwheat) made with no wheat binder, so the soba itself contains no wheat in the noodle.
Evening service centers on Japanese sake-bar small plates and sashimi, which conventionally use wheat-based soy sauce; no gluten-free soy sauce is mentioned.
Lunch curry can contain fish (e.g., a smoked-mackerel version) and the evening menu features sashimi and seafood, so shared preparation with animal products is likely.
Small owner-run counter where the proprietor personally explains the menu and sake to guests, so dietary questions can be discussed directly.

name: キヨ コラージュ (Kiyo courage)

claims.text: Guests are advised to inform staff of vegetarian or vegan preferences before ordering and to reserve in advance so the kitchen can accommodate; specific dairy, egg, and cross-contact details are not published and should be confirmed directly.
Vegetarian and partial vegan options can be prepared, and an English menu plus English-speaking staff have been reported, making it possible to discuss dietary needs.
The cooking centers on pesticide-free, organically grown vegetables delivered twice weekly from a trusted long-term grower.
Wheat noodles and a wheat-based soy sauce broth are central to every bowl, so a shared cooking environment makes the food unsuitable for gluten-free diners.
The ramen is a soy-sauce (shoyu) style broth, and standard Japanese soy sauce contains wheat.
The broth is pork-bone based and bowls are topped with char siu pork, so animal products are integral to the cooking, not just toppings.

name: Okonomiyaki Koguma (お好み焼き 仔ぐま)

claims.text: The shop also cooks standard wheat-based okonomiyaki and wheat soba/udon on the same teppan, so shared-surface cross-contact is a real risk; the GF/allergen-free versions are made to order and require reservation by the previous day.
GF okonomiyaki uses batter and noodles free of wheat flour and wheat-derived ingredients.
Okonomiyaki sauce is typically wheat-based; confirm the GF/allergen-free set uses a wheat-free sauce when reserving.

Owner developed allergen-free and gluten-free menus and offers custom combinations based on a customer's specific allergies; blood-glucose testing was run with hospital cooperation for the low-carb version.
One of very few shops in Japan offering a genuinely wheat-free Hiroshima-style okonomiyaki (batter + noodles), a dish that is otherwise a double wheat trap.

name: 小料理屋 永山 (Koryoriya Nagayama)

claims.text: Shared home-style kitchen with wheat-based soy sauce, miso preparations, and battered tempura onigiri fillings; no gluten-free protocol is documented, so cross-contamination should be assumed.
Side dishes and seasonings use Japanese soy sauce (standard shoyu is wheat-based), e.g. blanched bitter melon dressed in ponzu.
House dashi is made from bonito, tuna, and kombu, so vegetable miso soups and side dishes still contain fish stock; some miso soups also include pork.
Menu emphasizes fresh seasonal vegetables and several side dishes, and plain salt or umeboshi onigiri with nori are simple options, though none are prepared as certified allergen-free.
Okonomiyaki is built on a wheat-flour batter and cooked alongside wheat noodles on a shared teppan griddle, so cross-contact with gluten is unavoidable.
Dishes are finished with a Hiroshima okonomiyaki sauce, which is wheat-based; no wheat-free sauce is indicated.
The single griddle is used for pork, egg and seafood, so any vegetable-only order would share a surface with animal products.
広島風お好み焼きは小麦粉の生地と中華そばが基本で、同一の鉄板で複数の品を調理するため、グルテンの交差汚染は避けられない。グルテンフリー対応の記載は確認できなかった。
お好み焼きには小麦・魚介由来のお好みソースが使われるのが一般的で、本品も例外ではないと考えられる。小麦不使用ソースの提供情報は確認できなかった。
看板メニューに豚肉・卵・中華そば・かつお出汁が使われ、同じ鉄板で肉や卵を焼くため、植物性のみの調理を分離している情報は確認できなかった。
名物のハラペーニョトッピングやトルティーヤチップス等の中南米系サイドメニューがあり、ベジタリアン/ヴィーガンが食べられる品があるか店主に直接相談しやすい（店主は英語・スペイン語も通じやすい）。
